🇬🇧 UK Daily Briefing | Wednesday, 18 November 2026

1. 📈 UK inflation rises to 3.6%, its highest level in a year
Higher household energy bills and fuel costs have hit consumers since the war in Iran began in February.

2. 💼 Burnham promises to 'move quickly' on Milburn report on Neets
The prime minister told the BBC he wants to get 'stuck in' after the Milburn report proposed wide-ranging changes to help unemployed young people.

3. 🏥 NHS in England records over 3,000 snooping incidents in five years
Patient campaign groups and regulators called the figures 'deeply concerning'. They said the breaches distress patients and families and erode trust in the health service.

4. 📱 Ten teams will study social media ban's effect on youth mental health
Ten research teams will look at how well teenagers are coping without social media, in the largest British study of the ban's effect on youth mental health.

5. 🛂 Home Office publishes guidance on three new refugee sponsorship routes
The routes are named community sponsorship, refugee study and refugee work. They were first announced in the November 2025 asylum policy statement, Restoring Order and Control. Lead sponsor guidance was also published.

6. 🍽️ Supplies are critically low at 40% of food banks, Trussell warns
UK food banks are facing critically low levels of donations as they prepare for winter, according to a new report.

7. 🚗 UK would probably miss climate targets if EV sales rules are weakened
Analysis by the Climate Change Committee suggests the mooted move to let more petrol and diesel vehicles be sold would blow a hole in the plan to reach net zero by 2050.

8. 🎵 Harry Styles, Sam Fender and Billie Eilish will headline Glastonbury 2027
The festival will return after a fallow year with a pop-heavy line-up, led by Harry Styles and Cher.

Sources: The Independent, BBC, Guardian, Free Movement, Sky News. Stories summarised from UK media reports. Images: Pixabay. Photos: Raph_PH / CC BY 2.0, Wikimedia Commons.
